name: Imidafenacin

overview.mechanism: Antagonizes muscarinic receptors; assessed for reduction of overactive-bladder symptoms.
uses: Urinary urgency, frequency and urge incontinence associated with overactive bladder.

paragraphs.text: Taiwan FDA’s 2022 Uritos assessment supports symptomatic efficacy from Japanese and Taiwanese randomized trials. These are bladder-symptom outcomes; they do not establish kidney protection or efficacy in dialysis populations.

The assessment recommends caution in mild-to-moderate renal impairment and does not recommend use in severe renal impairment because of insufficient clinical data and the available tablet strength. It gives no numerical renal threshold or dialysis regimen; neither is inferred here.

Metabolism involves CYP3A4 and UGT1A4, with less than 10% of the dose recovered unchanged in urine. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers and additional anticholinergic medicines warrant attention. Reported risks include constipation, thirst, blurred vision, voiding difficulty, acute glaucoma and liver-enzyme elevation.

sources.citation: Taiwan Food and Drug Administration. Uritos (imidafenacin) 0.1 mg tablets assessment report; approval 22 June 2022, MOHW-PI 028330.

draft_notes: International reference sources do not establish the current Philippine-approved product instructions. No unsupported dialysis regimen added.
